title: Universal Data Workbench
summary: Import CSV and Parquet tables and inspect every column on this device: row counts, source and inferred types with their uncertainty, semantic roles that keep identifiers apart from measures, missing values, values that do not read, unusual values, suspected data errors and corrections that wait for approval, with a log of every conversion. Then every valid chart of a documented grammar is drawn for each table, each candidate accounted for as valid, excluded, failed or incomplete, with field, transformation, label, scale, layout and facet edits. Each table's hypotheses are tested by a documented catalogue with Benjamini–Yekutieli adjusted p-values, and its charts ranked in two lists, unusual patterns and statistically supported patterns, with six distinct highlights each explained. Any chart opens as a publication figure under the General, Nature or Science preset, at a size in millimetres, a resolution and a font of your choice, written as SVG, PDF with embedded TrueType text and PNG with its resolution recorded, each checked at its final size against the preset's dated rules. One download holds every valid figure with the report, specifications, statistics, a reproducibility manifest and a beamdswitch deck, and reopens as a project with its source hashes checked. Tables can be transformed with a SQL editor or visual controls that show their SQL, under a documented statement whitelist: each transformation keeps a record of its inputs, SQL, schema and rows in and out, with unmatched and duplicate join keys, and a selected result can be saved as a derived view or table or analysed as a table of its own. DuckDB 1.5.4 runs in the browser; files never leave the device. A preview: step 6 of 7.
